entries.title: Job 7:1
segments: Is there not a warfare to man upon earth? And are not his days like the days of a hireling?

entries.title: Job 7:2
segments: As a servant that earnestly desireth the shadow, And as a hireling that looketh for his wages:

entries.title: Job 7:3
segments: So am I made to possess months of misery, And wearisome nights are appointed to me.

entries.title: Job 7:4
segments: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? And I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.

entries.title: Job 7:5
segments: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; My skin closeth up, and breaketh out afresh.

entries.title: Job 7:6
segments: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, And are spent without hope.

entries.title: Job 7:7
segments: Oh remember that my life is a breath: Mine eye shall no more see good.

entries.title: Job 7:8
segments: The eye of him that seeth me shall behold me no more; Thine eyes shall be upon me, but I shall not be.

entries.title: Job 7:9
segments: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away, So he that goeth down to Sheol shall come up no more.

entries.title: Job 7:10
segments: He shall return no more to his house, Neither shall his place know him any more.

entries.title: Job 7:11
segments: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

entries.title: Job 7:12
segments: Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, That thou settest a watch over me?

entries.title: Job 7:13
segments: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, My couch shall ease my complaint;

entries.title: Job 7:14
segments: Then thou scarest me with dreams, And terrifiest me through visions:

entries.title: Job 7:15
segments: So that my soul chooseth strangling, And death rather than [these] my bones.

entries.title: Job 7:16
segments: I loathe [my life]; I would not live alway: Let me alone; for my days are vanity.

entries.title: Job 7:17
segments: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him, And that thou shouldest set thy mind upon him,

entries.title: Job 7:18
segments: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, And try him every moment?

entries.title: Job 7:19
segments: How long wilt thou not look away from me, Nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?

entries.title: Job 7:20
segments: If I have sinned, what do I unto thee, O thou watcher of men? Why hast thou set me as a mark for thee, So that I am a burden to myself?

entries.title: Job 7:21
segments: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust; And thou wilt seek me diligently, but I shall not be.
